newsitem.title: ITALY: Well-dressed imposter meets Pope at Vatican.
newsitem.headline: Well-dressed imposter meets Pope at Vatican.

text.p: A well-dressed imposter convinced officials that he was Mexico's new ambassador to the Vatican and met Pope John Paul at a general audience last week, Italian television reported on Wednesday.

Italian news bulletins broadcast footage of the March 19 audience showing the Spanish-speaking man, dressed smartly in a dark suit, being blessed with his wife and two teenage sons by the pontiff after the regular audience.

The unidentified man also tried to show the pontiff, who was seriously injured in an assassination attempt in St Peter's square at the Vatican by Turkish gunman Ali Agca in 1981, an assortment of photographs he had brought with him.
The Pope customarily meets a selection of people after general audiences in the Paul VI hall, spending a few seconds with each in turn and bestowing his blessing on them.
RAI television said the imposter knelt before the Pope, kissed his ring and then presented his family.
"I am the ambassador of Mexico," RAI quoted him as telling the Pope. It said the Pontiff blessed him and tried to turn to the next person waiting but the imposter lingered.

"The Pope, trying to free himself, blesses him again but the so-called diplomat hangs on, he re-presents his sons and goes down on his knees again. A master of ceremonies asks him politely to move on," the RAI commentary said.
There was no immediate comment from the Vatican.

The Italian news agency ANSA said the man had presented himself to officials before the audience and explained that he would be presenting his credentials to the Pope in a few days time but wanted to take part in the audience first.
"I'm at the Grand Hotel for the moment. You can find me there," it quoted him as telling officials. The agency said a later check with the Mexican embassy revealed the truth.
It was not the first time that imposters had got through tight security and presented themselves to Popes.
Television reports said that Vatican officials still remembered the time when a fake bishop presented himself to Pope Paul VI at his summer residence of Castel Gandolfo.
